title: You have no hut, You have no nest, You have no network, You are free from bonds. ( Blessed One ): I have no hut,…
content:
You have no hut,
You have no nest,
You have no network,
You are free from bonds.
( Blessed One ):
I have no hut,
I have no nest,
I have no network,
I am free from bonds.
( Devata ):
What do you call a hut?
What do you call a nest?
What do you call a network?
What do you call bonds?
( Blessed One ):
'Hut' is mother,
'Nest' is wife,
'Network' is children,
'Bonds' are craving.
( Devata ):
Good indeed, you have no hut!
Good indeed, you have no nest!
Good indeed, you have no network!
Good indeed, you are free from bonds!

title: Bhikkhus, just as at the end of the rainy season, in the autumn, when the crops are ripening, a cowherd, tending the cows, would strike…
content: Bhikkhus, just as at the end of the rainy season, in the autumn, when the crops are ripening, a cowherd, tending the cows, would strike the cows on this side and that with his stick, checking them and restraining them. Why is that? Because the cowherd sees that due to this he might incur death, imprisonment, beating, or blame. So too, bhikkhus, I saw the danger, the degradation, and the defilement of unwholesome states, and I saw the seclusion, the benefit, and the purification of wholesome states.

title: For them, the red-hot coals were extinguished, the smoke disappeared, the mortar and pestle fell askew. They ate in the evening for the evening meal,…
content: For them, the red-hot coals were extinguished, the smoke disappeared, the mortar and pestle fell askew. They ate in the evening for the evening meal, in the morning for the morning meal. They went into villages, towns, and capital cities for alms. Having obtained food, they returned to their leaf huts in the forest to practice meditation. Vāseṭṭha, they 'jhāyanti' (meditated), meaning they reflected. 'Jhāyaka' was the second name that arose.

title: - Bhikkhus, I will teach you suffering and the root of suffering. Listen ... Bhikkhus, what is suffering? Form, bhikkhus, is suffering; feeling is suffering;…
content: - Bhikkhus, I will teach you suffering and the root of suffering. Listen ... Bhikkhus, what is suffering? Form, bhikkhus, is suffering; feeling is suffering; perception is suffering; formations are suffering; consciousness is suffering. This, bhikkhus, is called suffering. Bhikkhus, what is the root of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, seeking delight here and there; that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence.

title: - This saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning, bhikkhus. A first point is not discerned of beings roaming and wandering on, shrouded by ignorance and fettered…
content: - This saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning, bhikkhus. A first point is not discerned of beings roaming and wandering on, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving. Just as, bhikkhus, a stick thrown up into the air sometimes falls on its base, sometimes in the middle, sometimes on its tip. So too, bhikkhus, beings shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving, roaming and wandering on, sometimes go from this world to another world, sometimes from another world to this world. Why is that? This saṃsāra is without discoverable beginning, bhikkhus ... enough to be liberated.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, among all kinds of woven cloth, a hair-blanket is considered the lowest. A hair-blanket, bhikkhus, is cold when it is cold, hot…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, among all kinds of woven cloth, a hair-blanket is considered the lowest. A hair-blanket, bhikkhus, is cold when it is cold, hot when it is hot, ugly, foul-smelling, and unpleasant to the touch. So too, bhikkhus, among the doctrines of the outside ascetics, the doctrine of Makkhali is considered the lowest. Bhikkhus, the foolish Makkhali has this view, this opinion: 'There is no action, no result of action, no striving.' Bhikkhus, those who were Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, Blessed Ones in the past, they all taught that there is action, that there is result of action, that there is striving. But, bhikkhus, the foolish Makkhali contradicts them all, saying: 'There is no action, no result of action, no striving.' Bhikkhus, those who will be Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, Blessed Ones in the future, they will all teach that there is action, that there is result of action, that there is striving. But, bhikkhus, the foolish Makkhali contradicts them all, saying: 'There is no action, no result of action, no striving.' And I myself, bhikkhus, now an Arahant, Perfectly Enlightened One, also teach that there is action, that there is result of action, that there is striving. But, bhikkhus, the foolish Makkhali contradicts me, saying: 'There is no action, no result of action, no striving.' Just as, bhikkhus, at the mouth of a river, someone sets a fish-trap, bringing misfortune, suffering, loss, and calamity to the fish. Just so, bhikkhus, at the mouth of a river, someone sets a fish-trap, bringing misfortune, suffering, loss, and calamity to the fish.

title: And, bhikkhus, how is a wrong-headed person in giving like a wrong-headed person? Here, bhikkhus, a wrong-headed person gives without respect, gives not with his…
content: And, bhikkhus, how is a wrong-headed person in giving like a wrong-headed person? Here, bhikkhus, a wrong-headed person gives without respect, gives not with his own hand, gives without careful consideration, gives things that are not needed, gives without regard for the future. Thus, bhikkhus, is a wrong-headed person in giving like a wrong-headed person.

title: Thus, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata has seen what is to be seen, but he does not conceive what is seen, does not conceive what is not…
content: Thus, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata has seen what is to be seen, but he does not conceive what is seen, does not conceive what is not seen, does not conceive what is to be seen, does not conceive a seer. He has heard what is to be heard, but he does not conceive what is heard, does not conceive what is not heard, does not conceive what is to be heard, does not conceive a hearer. He has sensed what is to be sensed, but he does not conceive what is sensed, does not conceive what is not sensed, does not conceive what is to be sensed, does not conceive a senser. He has cognized what is to be cognized, but he does not conceive what is cognized, does not conceive what is not cognized, does not conceive what is to be cognized, does not conceive a cognizer. Thus, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, regarding phenomena that are seen, heard, sensed, and cognized, is just thus. Moreover, beyond one who is thus, there is no one else more excellent or superior. So I declare.

title: Kevaddha, hearing this, I said to that bhikkhu: 'Bhikkhu, in the past, sea-merchants when sailing across the ocean would take along a land-sighting bird. When…
content:
Kevaddha, hearing this, I said to that bhikkhu: 'Bhikkhu, in the past, sea-merchants when sailing across the ocean would take along a land-sighting bird. When the ship had sailed far out and land was no longer visible, the merchants would release the land-sighting bird. The bird would fly east, south, west, north, upwards, and in intermediate directions. If it saw land all around, it would fly towards that land. If it did not see land all around, it would return to the ship. So too, bhikkhu, you have searched as far as the Brahmā realm without finding an answer to that question, so you have returned to me. Bhikkhu, the question should not be asked thus: "Venerable Sir, where do the four great elements — earth, water, fire, air — go after they have completely ceased?" Bhikkhu, the question should be asked thus: "Where do earth, water, fire, and air, long and short, fine and coarse, pure and impure, find no footing? Where do name-and-form completely cease?" And this is the answer to that question:

Consciousness is invisible, boundless, all-pervasive.
Here, earth, water, fire, wind element find no footing.
Here, also, long and short, fine and coarse, pure and impure.
Here, name and form completely cease.
When consciousness ceases, here everything ceases utterly.

title: Bhikkhus, what is Right Speech? Refraining from false speech, refraining from divisive speech, refraining from harsh speech, refraining from idle chatter. Bhikkhus, this is called…
content: Bhikkhus, what is Right Speech? Refraining from false speech, refraining from divisive speech, refraining from harsh speech, refraining from idle chatter. Bhikkhus, this is called Right Speech.
